pamphlet_excerpts: History Animation Old: The history of animation is as old as the history of storytelling.
Word Animate Means: The word animate means “alive.” When early humans firstpainted animals and hunting scenes on cave walls, they lit firesto show off their work.
Dancing Flames Cast: The dancing flames cast irregular light inthe caves, making the images of prehistoric animals appear tobe alive and moving.
Earliest Times Children: Also, from the earliest times, children worldwide have used a light source to project hand shadows onto a wall to create theshapes of animals.
step_by_step_procedure: Kind Entertainment Beenjoyed: This kind of entertainment can beenjoyed by a group of friends.
Shared Experience: The shared experience of creatinglifelike imitation is a key part of the attraction of animation.
Idea Projecting Shadows: The idea of projecting shadows led to the first magiclantern shows, starting around the mid to late 1700s and lastinguntil the introduction.
Primitive Projection: A primitive projection devicelike a wooden box with a candle inside was fitted with a lens.

pamphlet_excerpts: Principles Animation Basic: The principles of animation are a set of 12 basic ideas applied toanimation to create appealing, believable results.
They Wereintroduced Original: They wereintroduced by two of the original Disney animators, Ollie Johnston and Frank Thomas, in their book, Disney Animation: The Illusion.
Since Time Principles: Since that time, the principles havebecome standard in the animation industry.
Straight Ahead Action: Straight Ahead Action and Pose to Pose Straight-ahead action and pose to pose are the two mainmethods for animating.
step_by_step_procedure: Straight-ahead Action: Using straight-ahead action, theanimator draws or animates frame by frame, doing the drawingsin order: 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on.
Pose-to-pose Animation: With pose-to-pose animation, incontrast, the animator draws or poses the main (key) frames ofthe animation before filling in the in-between.
Thepose-to-pose Method: Using thepose-to-pose method, the animator might do drawing 1, thendrawing 25, and then drawing 47, before going back to do thedrawings.
Animators Pose-to-pose: Most animators use the pose-to-pose method becauseit offers benefits in timing and frame composition.

pamphlet_excerpts: Arethe Kinds Questions: These arethe kinds of questions you need to answer at thisstage of your planning.
Stopwatch Great Tool: A stopwatch is a great tool tohelp you estimate the time needed for the scene.
Afilm Video Reference: Afilm or video reference can be used to help guide yourdrawings.
Identify Key Character: To identify the key character poses you willneed, try shooting a reference with a video camera or a smartphone.
step_by_step_procedure: Play Back Video: Play back the video with a program thatlets you step through the frames one at a time.
Yourprogram Frame Counter: If yourprogram has a frame counter, take note of the framenumber of each pose for timing purposes.
Thumbnail Old Animation: Thumbnail is an old animation term for a small drawing notmuch larger than a person’s thumb.
Animators Createthese Tiny: Animators would createthese tiny drawings to help them visualize the key poses theywanted in their animations.
